title: Chapter 23 — The Voice in the Sand

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The fourth dawn rose the color of old copper.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek had not slept. The mark on his palm had throbbed through the night in time with his heartbeat, steady enough that the edges of the world felt thinner than they should. He kept the hand wrapped and told the others it was rope burn. They pretended to believe him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The donkeys had changed. By morning both animals refused the western slope of the dune where they had camped. They pulled against the ropes until the leather creaked, ears pinned flat. BAH-lahg crouched beside the nearer one and ran a hand down its neck. The animal trembled under his palm.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo snorted as she tightened the straps on her pack.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: They know they're donkeys. That's already more than most men.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg ignored her. He had spent enough years in the desert to trust what animals noticed first.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They broke camp without discussion and moved east. The donkeys settled once the western slope was behind them, though BAH-lahg kept glancing back. The desert stretched in every direction, a field of gold and red broken only by stone outcroppings and the skeletal remains of old caravan routes. The farther they traveled from Uruk, the less the world seemed to belong to people.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: By midmorning the heat pressed down through their clothing and wrapped itself around the backs of their necks. Zeek walked for part of the day to spare the animals. Ninsun rode in silence, filling the margins of her parchment with notes. She had stopped trying to hide what she was writing. The spiral-drop mark appeared again and again, copied from memory in different forms—some precise, some distorted, one containing a second shape buried inside the first.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: That's usually when things become expensive.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You say that as if everything can be reduced to a transaction.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They stopped shortly after midday beneath the thin shade of a half-buried rock spine. The stone gave barely enough cover for the four of them, but the sun had grown fierce enough that even a narrow strip of shadow felt like a gift.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek drank from his waterskin and immediately spat the water into the sand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Still tastes like it never saw the sun.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun took a careful sip from her own skin and stared at it.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Metallic. But not only iron. Something else is in it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one asked how he knew.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek watched the water darken the sand and vanish almost at once, as if the ground had drawn it down. For a moment the grains seemed to shift against one another. He blinked. The sand was still.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: How much water do we have left?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Enough if we reach the next well on schedule.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first sound came a few minutes later.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At first Zeek thought it was wind. The noise was so low he felt it more than heard it—a vibration passing through the stone beneath his hand. The dune beyond the rock spine shivered. Sand slipped down its slope in thin streams. Every grain around their boots began to tremble. Tiny ripples crossed the surface of every waterskin. The fire flattened, every flame leaning toward the earth as though something below were drawing breath.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The vibration continued, rising slowly, gathering beneath the silence of the desert. A low hum emerged, then another tone beneath it, then another. The sound seemed to come from everywhere at once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They reared against their ropes, eyes rolling white. BAH-lahg lunged for the nearest bridle. The second animal kicked wildly and nearly caught him in the chest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo's knife was in her hand before she seemed to realize she had drawn it. Zeek stood motionless.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The sound was no longer a hum. It was voices.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Thousands of them spoke over one another in a language that scraped against the inside of his skull. Some sounded close enough to touch. Others seemed to come from impossibly far away, buried beneath miles of stone and sand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun pressed both hands over her ears.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at her. Her face had gone pale.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.note: Whispered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark beneath the linen burned. The voices separated for one brief, terrible instant. Fragments reached him: his name, his father's name, the word lid, the word hunger. Then another word rose above the others—not spoken, but written across the inside of his mind.

lines.speaker: The City
lines.note: Not spoken; written across the inside of his mind. The City speaking: not fully human. Whispered, wet, close.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The silence that followed pressed harder than the noise had.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The donkeys continued trembling. BAH-lahg stood between them and the open desert, one hand on a bridle, the other on the haft of his axe. en-HEH-doo kept her knife raised. Ninsun slowly lowered her hands.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek answered. His own voice sounded strange to him.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at the desert. The dunes had not changed. The sky was clear. Nothing moved except the wind beginning to lift dust from the crest of the nearest ridge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They made camp early that evening. No one argued. The sun descended behind the dunes, turning the sky the color of tarnished metal. They built a small fire and kept the animals close. No one talked much.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Later, after the others had gone quiet, Zeek sat apart with the journal open across his knees. The stars above the desert were impossibly clear. He turned the pages.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A new entry had appeared on a page that had been blank the night before. The handwriting was his father's.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.note: Journal entry in Bel-iddin's hand; quietly ominous.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Below it, another line slowly darkened.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.note: Journal entry in Bel-iddin's hand; quietly ominous.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark beneath the linen began to pulse. Zeek looked toward the others—BAH-lahg asleep beside the donkeys, one hand still near his axe; en-HEH-doo with her knife beneath her arm; Ninsun curled under a blanket, notes scattered beside her.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: You should not have brought them.
lines.note: Journal entry in Bel-iddin's hand; quietly ominous.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's mouth went dry. He pressed his marked palm against the page. The journal shivered beneath his hand—not violently, not like an object being shaken, but like something alive responding to touch.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For a long moment he considered waking the others. Then the desert spoke.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The words came in his father's voice, but without his father's rhythm. Every pause was wrong. Every breath arrived half a heartbeat too late, as though something had reconstructed the sound from memory rather than ever having spoken it.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.note: CITY MIMIC of Bel-iddin's voice: every pause wrong, breaths half a beat late. Process: slight pitch drift, wet reverb.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: There was nothing behind him but darkness and sand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal remained open on his knees.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One word had replaced everything else.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.note: Journal entry in Bel-iddin's hand; quietly ominous.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A final line appeared beneath it.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.note: Journal entry in Bel-iddin's hand; quietly ominous.
